_meta.indication: INQOVI is indicated for treatment of adult patients with myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS), including previously treated and untreated, de novo and secondary MDS with the following FAB subtypes (refractory anemia, refractory anemia with ringed sideroblasts, refractory anemia with excess blasts, and chronic myelomonocytic leukemia [CMML]) and intermediate-1, intermediate-2, and high-risk International Prognostic Scoring System groups.

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, randomized, 2-cycle, 2-sequence crossover; patients randomized 1:1 to INQOVI (35 mg decitabine and 100 mg cedazuridine) orally in Cycle 1 and decitabine 20 mg/m2 IV in Cycle 2 or the reverse sequence.
pivotal_trials.population: 133 adult patients with MDS or CMML, including all FAB classification criteria and IPSS Intermediate-1, Intermediate-2, or high-risk prognostic scores.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary outcome measure was comparison of the 5-day cumulative decitabine AUC between INQOVI and intravenous decitabine; efficacy was established on the basis of complete response (CR) and rate of conversion from transfusion dependence to transfusion independence.
pivotal_trials.result: Geometric mean ratio for 5-day cumulative decitabine exposure between INQOVI and IV decitabine was 0.99 (90% CI: 0.93, 1.06). Complete Response 21% (95% CI: 15, 29); median duration of CR 7.5 months. 30 of 57 (53%) transfusion-dependent patients became transfusion-independent.

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, randomized, 2-cycle, 2-sequence crossover; patients randomized 1:1 to INQOVI (35 mg decitabine and 100 mg cedazuridine) orally in Cycle 1 and decitabine 20 mg/m2 IV in Cycle 2 or the reverse sequence.
pivotal_trials.population: 80 adult patients with MDS (IPSS Intermediate-1, Intermediate-2, or high-risk) or CMML.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Efficacy established on the basis of complete response (CR) and rate of conversion from transfusion dependence to transfusion independence.
pivotal_trials.result: Complete Response 18% (95% CI: 10, 28); median duration of CR 8.7 months. 20 of 41 (49%) transfusion-dependent patients became transfusion-independent.

key_safety: Fatal and serious myelosuppression can occur: thrombocytopenia 82% (Grade 3/4 76%), neutropenia 73% (Grade 3/4 71%), anemia 71% (Grade 3/4 55%), febrile neutropenia 33%. Most common adverse reactions (>=20%) include fatigue, constipation, hemorrhage, myalgia, mucositis, arthralgia, nausea, dyspnea, diarrhea, rash, dizziness, febrile neutropenia, edema, headache, cough, decreased appetite, upper respiratory tract infection, pneumonia, and transaminase increased.
target_moa: INQOVI combines decitabine, a nucleoside metabolic inhibitor that inhibits DNA methyltransferase causing hypomethylation of DNA and cellular differentiation/apoptosis, with cedazuridine, a cytidine deaminase (CDA) inhibitor that blocks the enzyme degrading decitabine in the GI tract and liver, thereby increasing oral bioavailability of decitabine.
modality: Small molecule (oral fixed-dose combination of two small-molecule nucleoside analogs: decitabine and cedazuridine)

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions.

description.text: Added INQOVI in combination with venetoclax for newly diagnosed AML in adults 75 or older or with comorbidities precluding intensive induction chemotherapy

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the indication of INQOVI in combination with venetoclax for the treatment of newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in adults 75 years or older, or who have comorbidities that preclude use of intensive induction chemotherapy.

orphan_indication.text: INQOVI has an orphan drug designation for this indication (MDS/CMML), which exempted the sponsor from the PREA pediatric assessment requirement.

citations.quote: Because this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.

basis.text: The NDA was reviewed under Priority review (PDUFA Goal Date August 11, 2020).

summary.text: NDA 212576 was received December 11, 2019 and reviewed as a Priority review application. The product has orphan drug designation for the MDS/CMML indication. It received regular (full) approval based on demonstration of equivalent 5-day decitabine exposure versus IV decitabine and supportive complete response and transfusion-independence data; it was not an accelerated approval and no advisory committee was convened.
